title: Rudder Trailing Edge Panel Bonding and Lightning Diverter Strip Renewal
abstract: Renewal of the diverter strip and the bonding path across the rudder trailing edge panels, following lightning attachment damage that repeatedly exceeded the allowable limit at the lower panel joints.

sections.reason: Seventeen lightning attachment events between 2014 and 2018 produced burn damage at the trailing edge panel joints that was beyond the allowable damage limit and required a panel change rather than a blend. In every case the attachment point was within eighty millimetres of a diverter strip termination. Analysis of the removed panels showed the strip terminating on a fastener that also carried a paint film, so the intended low resistance path into the fin structure was not present. The consequence for operators is a grounded aircraft waiting for a large composite panel and, in three cases, a ferry flight with a placard.
sections.description: The diverter strip is extended across the panel joint and terminated on a dedicated bonding lug rather than on a structural fastener. The forward plate D5540112864257 is replaced by an item with the lug boss machined in, and the right-hand doubler D5540116271167 is added under the termination so that the local laminate carries the strike current without delamination. The splice plate D5540117054490 is re-drilled to the new pattern and the fitting ZED693350-29 is refitted with titanium bolts AES706219-06 and countersunk washers AGS613028-9C. All eight terminations on both panels are treated. Work is on the rudder in zones 351, 353 and 355, with the surface removed and supported on a trestle, and the protective scheme is restored to the standard practice for a bonded joint.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 3.2 kg on the rudder, aft of the hinge line, which is inside the existing mass balance tolerance but must be recorded because the rudder is a balanced surface. No electrical load change. Not interchangeable: the panel and the doubler must be embodied together. The lightning bonding resistance check gains two measurement points and its limit tightens. Structure repair content for the trailing edge panel changes because the repair scheme must now respect the strip routing.
sections.embodiment_note: Production cut-in at MSN S01355. Retrofit is a rudder-off task and is offered only at a heavy check; ninety-six manhours with two people and a fin access platform. Panels removed at retrofit are scrapped, not returned.

type_data.balance_impact: Aft of the rudder hinge line; inside the mass balance tolerance but recorded
type_data.production_impact: Cut-in at MSN S01355; panel supplier tooling change required
